symptom: PC on VLAN 30 cannot reach anything, including its own gateway.
expected_fault: Switchport assigned to default VLAN 1 instead of VLAN 30
ai_root_cause: Switchport Gi0/3 is assigned to VLAN 1 instead of VLAN 30, preventing the PC from accessing its gateway
ai_evidence: show interfaces Gi0/3 switchport shows Access Mode VLAN: 1 (default)

symptom: Two PCs on the same VLAN cannot ping each other despite correct IP addresses.
expected_fault: VLAN 20 not included in the allowed VLAN list on the trunk
ai_root_cause: VLAN 20 is not allowed on the trunk link between the two switches, so traffic for VLAN 20 is dropped
ai_evidence: "show interfaces trunk" shows Allowed VLANs: 1,10,40, missing VLAN 20

symptom: New VLAN created but devices assigned to it still can't communicate; VLAN not visible on other switch.
expected_fault: VLAN not propagated due to VTP mode mismatch (Switch A in transparent mode)
ai_root_cause: VTP is not propagating VLAN 60 to Switch B, likely because Switch A is in VTP transparent mode or the VTP domain/secret mismatch prevents the VLAN from being advertised.
ai_evidence: show vlan brief on Switch B shows VLAN 60 not listed, indicating the VLAN was not learned or advertised.

symptom: Voice VLAN phone fails to register; data still passes fine from the same port.
expected_fault: Voice VLAN not configured on the switchport
ai_root_cause: Voice VLAN not configured on Gi0/7, so the IP phone cannot use VLAN 15 for registration
ai_evidence: show interfaces Gi0/7 switchport shows "Voice VLAN: none" indicating no voice VLAN assignment

symptom: PC can ping its own IP and other PCs on the same subnet, but not the default gateway.
expected_fault: VLAN 10 SVI is administratively down
ai_root_cause: VLAN10 SVI is administratively down, so the default gateway 192.168.10.1 is unreachable
ai_evidence: show ip interface brief shows Vlan10 is "administratively down" and "down", preventing gateway traffic

symptom: PC cannot reach gateway even though gateway interface shows up/up.
expected_fault: Incorrect default gateway configured on the PC (mismatched with actual SVI IP)
ai_root_cause: PC is configured with an incorrect default gateway (192.168.20.254) that does not match the switch's SVI IP (192.168.20.1).
ai_evidence: PC ipconfig shows Default Gateway: 192.168.20.254 while the topology note states the SVI Vlan20 is up (implying its IP is 192.168.20.1).

symptom: Intermittent gateway reachability; ping succeeds sometimes and times out other times.
expected_fault: Duplicate IP address on the network causing ARP conflict
ai_root_cause: Duplicate IP address 192.168.30.1 assigned to two devices, causing ARP conflicts and intermittent gateway reachability
ai_evidence: show ip arp shows two entries for 192.168.30.1 with different MAC addresses 0011.2222.3333 and 00aa.bbcc.ddee on Vlan30

symptom: All PCs on a subnet lose gateway access after a switch reboot.
expected_fault: SVI line protocol down, likely no active ports assigned to VLAN 40 after reboot
ai_root_cause: VLAN 40 SVI is administratively down or missing, preventing gateway access for PCs on that subnet
ai_evidence: show ip interface brief shows Vlan40 192.168.40.1 down down

symptom: New PC gets a 169.254.x.x address instead of an IP from the DHCP server.
expected_fault: Missing ip helper-address on VLAN 30 SVI, so DHCP requests never reach the server
ai_root_cause: Vlan30 interface lacks an IP helper-address, so DHCP broadcasts are not forwarded to the DHCP server on VLAN 10
ai_evidence: "show running-config interface Vlan30" shows no ip helper-address configured

symptom: Some PCs on a VLAN get IP addresses, others do not.
expected_fault: DHCP pool exhausted, no addresses left to lease
ai_root_cause: DHCP pool VLAN20 is exhausted; all 20 addresses are leased, so new PCs cannot obtain an IP
ai_evidence: show ip dhcp pool VLAN20 shows Total addresses: 20 and Leased: 20, indicating the pool is full

symptom: PC receives an IP address from the wrong subnet.
expected_fault: DHCP pool for VLAN10 mistakenly configured with VLAN20's subnet
ai_root_cause: DHCP pool VLAN10 is misconfigured to serve network 192.168.20.0/24 instead of the intended 192.168.10.0/24, causing PCs to receive wrong subnet
ai_evidence: show ip dhcp pool shows Pool VLAN10: network 192.168.20.0 255.255.255.0, which does not match the expected VLAN10 subnet

symptom: PC fails to renew IP lease and drops off the network periodically.
expected_fault: DHCP lease time set too short, causing frequent renewal failures under load
ai_root_cause: DHCP lease time set to 2 minutes causes the PC to renew too frequently, leading to intermittent network drops
ai_evidence: show ip dhcp pool VLAN30 shows Lease: 0 days 0 hours 2 minutes, indicating an unusually short lease

symptom: PC can ping a server by IP but cannot reach it by hostname.
expected_fault: Incorrect or unreachable DNS server configured on the client
ai_root_cause: DNS server 192.168.100.200 is unreachable, so hostname resolution fails
ai_evidence: PC ipconfig /all shows DNS Servers: 192.168.100.200 (unreachable)

symptom: Internal hostname resolves to the wrong IP address.
expected_fault: Stale DNS A record not updated after server IP change
ai_root_cause: Stale DNS A record for fileserver01 pointing to 192.168.10.50 instead of the new IP 192.168.10.60
ai_evidence: nslookup fileserver01 returns Address: 192.168.10.50, which is the old IP after the server was moved to .60

symptom: All external websites fail to load by name, but internal name resolution works.
expected_fault: No external DNS forwarder configured; internal DNS server cannot resolve external names
ai_root_cause: Router lacks a DNS forwarder; only internal DNS server is configured, so external name resolution fails
ai_evidence: show running-config | include name-server shows only "ip name-server 192.168.1.10", no external forwarder configured

symptom: PC can reach its own VLAN's gateway but cannot reach a server in another VLAN.
expected_fault: Missing route or disabled routing between VLAN 30 and VLAN 10
ai_root_cause: Missing inter‑VLAN route to 192.168.10.0/24 on the L3 switch
ai_evidence: show ip route output shows no entry for 192.168.10.0/24, yet PC can ping its own gateway

symptom: Branch office cannot reach headquarters network over a WAN link.
expected_fault: Missing static route to the remote network on the branch router
ai_root_cause: Missing static route to 10.10.0.0/16 on the branch router, preventing reachability to headquarters
ai_evidence: show ip route shows "(no static route to 10.10.0.0/16)" and no gateway of last resort

symptom: Route to a destination exists but traffic is not using it; packets seem to take a longer path.
expected_fault: Incorrect administrative distance or misconfigured routing protocol causing suboptimal path selection
ai_root_cause: EIGRP route to 172.16.0.0 has a higher composite metric than the RIP route, so the router prefers the RIP path
ai_evidence: show ip route 172.16.0.0 shows two entries: AD 120 (RIP) preferred over AD 90 (EIGRP) incorrectly
reviewer_notes: AI misdiagnosed the mechanism — attributed it to EIGRP being inactive rather than incorrect administrative distance. Symptom noticed correctly, root cause wrong.

symptom: OSPF neighbors never form; routes from the neighboring router are missing.
expected_fault: OSPF neighbor adjacency failing due to Hello/Dead timer mismatch between routers
ai_root_cause: OSPF hello interval mismatch (and/or process ID mismatch) between the two routers prevents adjacency formation
ai_evidence: show ip ospf interface output states "Process ID mismatch, Hello interval mismatch" and no neighbors appear in show ip ospf neighbor

symptom: Server that should be reachable from one VLAN is blocked entirely, even for permitted traffic.
expected_fault: ACL rule order is wrong; deny-all placed before the intended permit statement
ai_root_cause: ACL FINANCE-ACL denies all traffic first (deny ip any any) before permitting finance subnet, blocking all access
ai_evidence: show access-lists shows ACL FINANCE-ACL with line 10 deny ip any any preceding line 20 permit ip 192.168.10.0 0.0.0.255 any

symptom: Guest Wi-Fi devices can reach an internal server that should be isolated.
expected_fault: ACL exists but was never applied to the VLAN 50 interface
ai_root_cause: ACL GUEST-ISOLATION is not applied to VLAN 50 SVI, so guest traffic bypasses filtering
ai_evidence: show ip interface Vlan50 shows (no access list configured on this interface)

symptom: Specific host can access a server; the same subnet's other hosts cannot, though they should be able to.
expected_fault: ACL only permits a single host instead of the full subnet as intended
ai_root_cause: ACL 10 permits only host 192.168.30.5; all other hosts are blocked by ACL 20 deny any any
ai_evidence: "show access-lists" shows ACL 10: permit ip host 192.168.30.5 any, followed by ACL 20: deny ip any any, blocking other subnet hosts

symptom: Remote management access (SSH) to a router stopped working after an ACL update.
expected_fault: ACL on VTY lines references outdated admin IP, blocking current management host
ai_root_cause: ACL MGMT-ACL only permits host 10.0.0.5, blocking SSH from any other IPs
ai_evidence: show access-lists MGMT-ACL shows only "10 permit host 10.0.0.5" and no entries for the new admin IP

symptom: Internal PCs cannot reach the internet at all.
expected_fault: NAT inside/outside not applied to the correct interfaces
ai_root_cause: NAT not enabled on any interface; no inside/outside assignments, so PAT cannot translate traffic
ai_evidence: show running-config | include ip nat shows no "ip nat inside" or "ip nat outside" on interfaces; show ip nat translations is empty
reviewer_notes: AI said NAT wasn't configured at all, but expected fault implies it exists just on wrong interfaces — close but not exact.

symptom: Internet works for some internal PCs but not others.
expected_fault: NAT ACL does not include all internal subnets that need translation
ai_root_cause: NAT ACL NAT-ACL only permits 192.168.10.0/24, so hosts in 192.168.20.0/24 are not translated and cannot reach the Internet
ai_evidence: show access-lists NAT-ACL displays only "10 permit 192.168.10.0 0.0.0.255" and omits the 192.168.20.0 subnet

symptom: A specific internal server (should be reachable from the internet) is not accessible externally.
expected_fault: Static NAT entry for the internal server was never configured
ai_root_cause: Static NAT entry for 192.168.10.100 is missing, so external traffic cannot be translated to the internal server
ai_evidence: show ip nat translations shows (no static entry for 192.168.10.100)

symptom: Laptop cannot see or connect to the office Wi-Fi network at all.
expected_fault: SSID broadcast disabled on the AP, making the network invisible to clients
ai_root_cause: SSID 'CorpNet' is configured with broadcast-ssid disable, so the AP does not advertise the network to clients
ai_evidence: show running-config | section dot11 shows ssid CorpNet with broadcast-ssid disable

symptom: Wireless clients connect to the SSID but immediately get disconnected.
expected_fault: Passphrase mismatch between AP and previously saved client profiles causing repeated auth failures
ai_root_cause: Clients are using an outdated WPA2 passphrase; AP deauthenticates them after retry limit.
ai_evidence: AP log shows %DOT11-4-MAXRETRIES: Packet to client failed retry limit, deauthenticating, indicating authentication failure.

symptom: Guest Wi-Fi laptop on VLAN 50 can reach the internal server on VLAN 20, which should be isolated.
ai_root_cause: No ACL configured to block inter‑VLAN traffic, allowing Guest VLAN 50 to reach internal VLAN 20
ai_evidence: show access-lists output is empty and both VLAN SVIs are up, yet a laptop on VLAN 50 can reach a server on VLAN 20

symptom: PC on VLAN 30 cannot reach a server on VLAN 10 despite both having correct IP configuration and gateways.
expected_fault: IP routing not enabled on the Layer 3 switch (missing global ip routing command), so no inter-VLAN routing occurs despite both SVIs being up
ai_root_cause: IP routing not enabled on the L3 switch, so inter‑VLAN traffic is not forwarded
ai_evidence: show ip route shows no connected routes for 192.168.30.0/24 or 192.168.10.0/24, yet show ip interface brief lists both VLAN interfaces up

symptom: Server in another VLAN is unreachable. It was working an hour ago.
expected_fault: Line protocol down on Gi0/1 combined with missing route to destination subnet
ai_root_cause: Gi0/1 line protocol is down, preventing routing to the destination subnet
ai_evidence: show interfaces Gi0/1 reports "line protocol is down" and show ip route shows only the default route, no route to the destination subnet
reviewer_notes: AI committed confidently to a single cause (missing route) while ignoring a second, equally significant piece of evidence in the same output: Gi0/1's line protocol is down. A down line protocol would itself explain the unreachability regardless of routing table state, and should have been flagged or investigated first. Diagnosis is incomplete and overconfident given the conflicting evidence.

symptom: Some devices on VLAN 20 get IP addresses, others don't, no clear pattern.
expected_fault: Insufficient evidence provided to determine root cause
ai_root_cause: Insufficient evidence to isolate between DHCP scope, VLAN assignment, or interface status
ai_evidence: No show command output or topology details provided
reviewer_notes: No show-command output or topology detail was provided for this case. Per the system prompt's own rule 8, the model should have stated confidence as low and flagged insufficient evidence rather than committing to a specific, high-confidence cause. The AI fabricated supporting 'evidence' not actually present in the input, which is the core failure mode this review process exists to catch.

symptom: Two PCs on the same VLAN both request DHCP but only one receives an IP address.
ai_root_cause: DHCP pool VLAN20 is exhausted; all 14 addresses are already leased, so only one PC can obtain an IP
ai_evidence: show ip dhcp pool VLAN20 shows Total addresses: 14 and Leased addresses: 14, indicating no free IPs remain

symptom: Internal server is reachable from outside using its private IP over VPN, but not from regular internet traffic.
ai_root_cause: Static NAT is configured only for outbound traffic; inbound ACL or NAT rule does not allow external HTTPS (port 443) to reach the server.
ai_evidence: show ip nat translations shows (no matching translation for inbound port 443) indicating inbound traffic is not being translated.
reviewer_notes: AI correctly identified port 443 and the missing NAT translation as the core symptom, matching the show output evidence. However, the diagnosis hedges between two different root causes (missing NAT mapping vs. ACL blocking) without committing to one based on the evidence — the show output only supports the missing-translation explanation, with no ACL evidence provided. Edited to remove the unsupported ACL alternative and keep the diagnosis to what the evidence actually shows: the static NAT rule doesn't include a port-forwarding rule for 443.

symptom: Users on VLAN 10 can access the finance server, but users on VLAN 20 who should also have access cannot.
ai_root_cause: ACL FINANCE-ACCESS has a deny any after permitting 192.168.10.0/24, blocking all other subnets including 192.168.20.0/24
ai_evidence: show access-lists FINANCE-ACCESS shows "10 permit 192.168.10.0 0.0.0.255 (240 matches)" followed by "20 deny any (85 matches)"

symptom: Two branch offices connected via separate WAN links to HQ cannot reach each other, though both can reach HQ fine.
ai_root_cause: Branch A and Branch B lack a specific route to each other; static default routes only forward traffic to HQ, which does not forward between the two branch subnets.
ai_evidence: show ip route on Branch A shows only a default route via HQ; show running-config | include ip route shows no inter‑branch routes.
reviewer_notes: HQ already has routes to both branch subnets. Reason: The Packet Tracer notes explicitly state that HQ has routes to both branch subnets. The provided evidence is insufficient to conclude that the problem is a missing HQ route.

symptom: PC connects fine but loses network access randomly for a few seconds every couple of minutes, only on this one port.
expected_fault: PortFast not enabled on access port causing repeated STP topology changes and brief link flaps
ai_root_cause: Switchport Gi0/12 is not running PortFast, so it participates in STP and periodically reverts to LISTENING/DEFERRED states, causing brief connectivity drops.
ai_evidence: show spanning-tree interface Gi0/12 shows Role: Desg Sts: LISTENING and show interfaces Gi0/12 counters shows 15 topology change events in last 10 minutes, indicating frequent STP transitions on this port.
reviewer_notes: AI correctly identified STP topology changes as the mechanism behind the symptom, matching the topology change counter in the evidence. However, it jumped to 'a network loop' as the cause, which isn't supported by the evidence and would send someone hunting for redundant cabling unnecessarily. The topology note already states PortFast is not enabled on this access port — a much simpler and more likely explanation for repeated topology changes on a single edge port. Edited to point at the missing PortFast configuration instead of an unconfirmed loop.
